title: Where kamma is made
hookLine: wholesome, unwholesome, resultant and functional states of mind
carry: results arrive; kamma is made in the response

lines: THE MIND, ON THE BENCH ALL WEEK.
cards: All week, the mind has been on the bench, taken apart piece by piece, the way a watchmaker lays out a watch. Today, one more way of sorting, and it's the one that ties the week together.
Every moment of mind, the Abhidhamma says, belongs to one of four families. Two of them are familiar. The other two are where it gets interesting.

teach.b: The commentaries give the word several shades: healthy, blameless, skillful, and bringing good results. A wholesome moment is rooted in generosity, kindness, or understanding.
Second, the unwholesome family, akusala: moments rooted in greed, aversion, or confusion. These first two are the families that act. They're the eating under the mango tree, where kamma is made.
Third, the resultant family, vipaka: the ripening of earlier actions. And here's the surprise. The manuals count bare seeing, hearing, smelling and tasting as resultant.
When a rude message lands on your phone, the simple seeing of the words isn't a deed at all. It's a result, arriving.
The acting comes after, in what the mind does with it. Fourth, the functional family, kiriya. These moments do a job and leave no seed behind.
The moment that turns the mind toward the crash in the next room is functional: it just turns. And the manuals say this about the awakened.
When an arahant, one who has fully woken up, acts with kindness, the moment is counted as functional. It does its work, it helps, and it plants nothing more.
So the four families aren't a scorecard for sorting yourself into good or bad. They're a map of where the choosing happens. Results arrive.

teach.h: KAMMA IS MADE IN THE RESPONSE.
teach.b: And in between, at the response, a moment comes out wholesome or unwholesome: the narrow place where something can change.

how: Abhidhamma students in Theravada communities learn to classify each kind of consciousness as wholesome, unwholesome, resultant or functional, and teachers use the scheme to show where kamma is made.

games.q: a rude message lands on your phone. you see the words. which family is that bare seeing in?
games.why: the manuals count bare seeing as resultant, vipaka. it's not where you act. wholesome or unwholesome comes after, in what the mind does with it.

practice: If you'd like, sit and wait until something arrives, a sound, a memory, an itch, and let it arrive; that's a result.
Then watch what the mind does next, and if anything kind, patient, generous or clear turns up, even faintly, just see it. There's no need to make one happen; noticing one is the practice.

wordCard.voice: Four families. Wholesome, unwholesome, resultant and functional: four ways the Abhidhamma sorts every moment of mind. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali: wholesome; the commentaries give shades like healthy, blameless, skillful.

carryVoice: Your line: results arrive; kamma is made in the response. A week on the bench, complete.
